t: Specification parsing into a build frame (foundational)
title: Specification parsing into a build frame (foundational)
description: The natural-language specification is parsed into a build frame: function name, inputs with types, outputs with types, and behavior examples. Parsing is strict: an underspecified frame is returned for clarification rather than built on guesses. The frame is the contract the generated tool must satisfy. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Tool Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

t: Code synthesis from the build frame (foundational)
title: Code synthesis from the build frame (foundational)
description: Code is synthesized from the frame using templates for common shapes: transformers, filters, aggregators, and validators. Template-based synthesis keeps generated code readable and reviewable, unlike opaque model output. The synthesized module includes docstrings drawn from the specification text. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Tool Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Test generation from spec examples (foundational)
description: The specification's examples become executable tests automatically, each asserting the example's expected output. Edge cases are added from the input types: empty inputs, boundary values, and wrong types. Generated tests are the acceptance suite the tool must pass. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
examples = [('a b', 2), ('', 0)]
def wordcount(t): return len(t.split())
results = [(inp, wordcount(inp) == want) for inp, want in examples]
print('generated tests:', results, '| all pass:', all(r[1] for r in results))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Tool Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Validation gate before deployment (foundational)
description: The synthesized tool must pass its generated tests plus the adversarial-content detector's code scan before it can deploy. The gate is non-negotiable: no passing tests, no deployment, no exceptions. Gate results are logged with the tool's version for audit. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
tests_pass, scan_clean = True, True
print('deployment gate:', 'OPEN' if (tests_pass and scan_clean) else 'CLOSED')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Tool Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Deployment packaging with metadata (foundational)
description: The validated tool is packaged with metadata: name, version, capability tags, the spec it was built from, and its test results. Packaging registers the tool in the registry so the capability matcher can discover it. The package is immutable once published; fixes become new versions. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
pkg = {'name': 'wordcount', 'version': '1.0.0', 'caps': ['count', 'text'], 'tests': '4/4 pass'}
print('published:', pkg['name'], pkg['version'], '|', pkg['tests'])
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Tool Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
